title: Grocery search that understands how people type
summary: Find the right product when a person types in Kanglish, misspells it or names a local brand.
context: Malleshwaram Mart delivers groceries from 80 dark stores. A shopper may type 'tuppa', 'ghee', 'gee' or 'nandini tuppa' and expects the same shelf. Stock and price differ from store to store and change through the day.

Search is the first thing most shoppers touch. A third of searches now return nothing or something unrelated, and those shoppers tend to leave. There are 120,000 products and about 300 searches a second at the evening peak.
must_handle: Spelling mistakes and Kannada words written in English find the right item.
A result out of stock at this person's store is not shown as available.
Results come back in about 150 ms at the evening peak.
A merchandiser can change ranking without a deploy.
A new product is searchable within a few minutes.
show_in_answer: How the index is built, and what goes in it.
How one search runs from text to ranked results.
Where stock and price join in, and what is cached and for how long.
How you would know that a ranking change made things better.
